title: Warp one word onto another
brief: Build the DTW table with a Sakoe-Chiba band, read the warping path back from it, and recognize noisy synthetic words by their nearest template.
hints: local_cost broadcasts: a[:, None, :] - b[None, :, :] has shape (n, m, d); square, sum over the last axis, and take the square root.
In accumulated_cost, fill D row by row. Treat a neighbor with i - 1 < 0 or j - 1 < 0 as np.inf, and treat (0, 0) as having a predecessor of cost 0.
A forbidden cell keeps np.inf, so any path through it costs infinity and min() steers around it without a special case.
backtrack walks from the last cell to (0, 0), each time taking the cheapest of the three predecessors that exist, then reverses the list.
classify compares distance / len(path), not the raw distance: a raw DTW distance grows with the length of the template.
